title: Compu Methods
$comment: Computation methods, one file each under `data_types/compu_methods/`: how a stored value becomes the physical or the named one, an element a type names by reference. Two element kinds discriminated by `kind` (`texttable`, `linear`), plus one nested member kind (`table_entry`). An enumeration, a value type and a reference type name a `texttable` by their `compu_method_ref`, an application type names a `linear` by its own. The directory is mandatory and may be empty.

oneOf.description: A computation method of category `TEXTTABLE`, emitted as a `COMPU-METHOD` in `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`: a table of named values, one closed single-point `COMPU-SCALE` per entry, the shape an enumeration's own generated method has. An enumeration names one by its `compu_method_ref` in place of inline `literals`, and an implementation value or reference type by its `compu_method_ref`, which is the one way an implementation type states literals.

name.description: The compu method's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/compu_methods/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the compu methods, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name.

kind.description: The discriminator that selects this compu method kind; always `texttable`.

entries.description: The table's named values, addressed by `name`, in the order they are emitted. Must not be empty: a `TEXTTABLE` holds one or more scales.

description.description: Free text about the compu method. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

package.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`, its layer's package, this compu method is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the compu method and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/CompuMethods/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/CompuMethods` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

oneOf.description: A computation method of category `LINEAR`, emitted as a `COMPU-METHOD` in `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`: physical = stored × `factor` + `offset`, one `COMPU-SCALE` in the internal-to-physical direction, referring to the `unit` element it names. An application type names one by its `compu_method_ref`, in place of an inline `conversion`. It holds no scale label, which the standard makes not applicable for a `LINEAR` scale; the scale's limits are its optional `limits`.

name.description: The compu method's identity; the file is named from it (`data_types/compu_methods/{name}.yaml`, or a suffixed name when another file collides case-insensitively) and is never what identifies it. Unique across the compu methods, must not be blank, and immutable; an element of another layer may carry the same name.

kind.description: The discriminator that selects this compu method kind; always `linear`.

unit.description: The name of the declared unit, an element of the `units` layer, the method refers to: a `LINEAR` computation method refers to a unit. Must not be blank.

factor.description: The multiplier applied to the stored value. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float.

offset.description: The constant added after the multiplication. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float.

limits.description: The limits of the linear computation method's scale, on the stored side: the values the conversion is defined for, which is what the standard reads a scale's limits as -- the limiting values before the conversion is applied. Written as the scale's `LOWER-LIMIT` and `UPPER-LIMIT`. Absent, the scale states no limit and the conversion applies to every stored value; it is not the physical range, which is the type's `range`.

description.description: Free text about the compu method. Written into the generated ARXML as the element's `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.

package.description: The one sub-package of `/DataTypes/CompuMethods`, its layer's package, this compu method is emitted in, a single SHORT-NAME segment: the compu method and every reference to it take `/DataTypes/CompuMethods/{package}/`. Absent means `/DataTypes/CompuMethods` itself. It is held to the AUTOSAR Identifier rule.

linear_limits.description: The limits of a linear computation method's scale, on the stored side. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change. Either limit may be left out; the lower one must not be above the upper one, and the two may be equal only when both are closed.

lower.description: The lowest stored value the conversion applies to, written as the scale's `LOWER-LIMIT`; omitted or `null` when the scale states none. An infinite limit is no bound: leave it out.

upper.description: The highest stored value the conversion applies to, written as the scale's `UPPER-LIMIT`; omitted or `null` when the scale states none. An infinite limit is no bound: leave it out.

linear_limit_bound.description: One limit of a scale: a stored value and whether the limit itself belongs to the interval. A nested object rather than a list member, so it has no identity of its own and every field of it may change.

value.description: The limit's stored value. An integer is held as the integer it is, never rounded through a float; it accepts neither NaN nor ±Infinity.

interval.description: Whether the limit belongs to the interval: `closed` (it does; the default, as an absent `INTERVAL-TYPE` is) or `open` (it does not). Written as the limit's `INTERVAL-TYPE`.

table_entry.description: One named value of a `texttable`: a member of its `entries` collection, never a standalone element, so it has no file and no layer-level address. It has an enum literal's shape.

name.description: The entry's identity inside its table, written as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `SHORT-LABEL` and its `VT`, exactly as an enum literal's name; must not be blank, and immutable.

value.description: The integer the entry stands for, emitted as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `LOWER-LIMIT` and `UPPER-LIMIT`.

description.description: Free text about the entry. Written into the generated ARXML as its `COMPU-SCALE`'s `DESC`, exactly as held; the empty default writes none.
